## Why This Process Is Required

The project has a PM-confirmed actual launch date, historical conditional targets that have passed, an outdated current schedule view, and remaining operational and quality controls with no dated post-launch sequence. A schedule-control refresh is needed to compare the actual milestone with the recorded targets and to provide a usable working forecast without inventing a baseline.

## Tailoring Factors

| Factor | Project evidence | Tailoring effect |
|---|---|---|
| Criticality | The application is live and post-launch operational controls remain open | Use a short hypercare window and an explicit evidence review point |
| Duration | The immediate control horizon is the period after the 2026-09-15 launch | Use rolling windows through a proposed 2026-09-26 review |
| Complexity | Gate 1, operations, responsive acceptance, logging, bot-abuse controls, reminder evidence, and deployment decisions are linked | Show sequencing and predecessors, not dates alone |
| Resources | Dennis Arquillano and Agno JF are recorded for some existing controls; other owners remain TBD or Unassigned | Preserve existing owners and do not assign missing owners |
| Approach | The project uses iterative delivery with unresolved target-environment evidence | Use a working forecast and evidence-triggered replanning rather than a baseline |
| Maturity | An approved schedule-management plan exists, but the project schedule and milestone list were not previously maintained as a current carrier | Create one combined working schedule and milestone carrier and update the method trigger |

## Minimum Output

1. Record the actual 2026-09-15 launch milestone and its comparison with historical or conditional targets.
2. Create a dated post-launch working plan for hypercare and remaining controls.
3. Show dependencies, owners as currently recorded, evidence requirements, and the next review trigger.
4. Preserve the no-retrospective-baseline direction and identify what remains unavailable for formal variance analysis.
5. Reconcile only the approved schedule artifact, schedule-method metadata, dashboard view, artifact index, and process metadata; do not change item states or owners.

## Trigger And Review Point

The run is triggered by the PM approval on 2026-09-17 following the schedule-domain review. The launch actual is 2026-09-15. The working review point is proposed for 2026-09-26 after the first hypercare window and the refreshed Gate 1 and operational evidence.

## Authority Boundary

The PM approved the schedule refresh and explicitly excluded a retrospective baseline. The run may record the actual launch and create a non-baselined working schedule. It may not assign owners, close or change register items, change external source documents, establish a baseline, or convert proposed future windows into committed dates without separate direction.

## Candidate Artifact Scope

The PM-18 artifact candidates are filtered in Stage 02. The plan uses the existing schedule-management plan, combines the activity and milestone views into one project-schedule carrier, defers calendars and the baseline, and keeps visual or utilization views generated on demand unless a later decision requires them.
